claims.text: Atomic-scale lattice distortion in CoCrFeMnNi produces heterogeneous local shear-modulus domains.
Heterogeneous local shear-modulus domains pin dislocations more effectively under dynamic loading.
Heterogeneous local shear-modulus domains promote dislocation multiplication under dynamic loading.
Enhanced dislocation pinning and multiplication increase strain-rate sensitivity and dynamic strength without reducing ductility.
The proposed HEA is equimolar CoCrFeMnNi.
The proposed HEA is annealed to a homogeneous microstructure.
The proposed HEA has an average grain size of approximately 10 µm.
The proposed HEA has a dislocation density of approximately 10^12 m^-2.
Increasing strain rate makes dislocations interact more frequently with high-local-shear-modulus regions.
More frequent interaction with high-local-shear-modulus regions enhances dislocation pinning and multiplication.
Enhanced pinning and multiplication increase dynamic yield strength.
Enhanced pinning and multiplication increase work hardening.
Relative to microstructurally matched pure Ni, CoCrFeMnNi will have 10–20% higher dynamic yield strength throughout the tested strain-rate range.
Relative to pure Ni, CoCrFeMnNi will have a strain-rate-sensitivity coefficient m higher by approximately 0.05–0.1.
The total ductility of CoCrFeMnNi will remain within 10% of that of pure Ni.
The proposed mechanism is expected to hold from strain rates of 10^-3 to 10^3 s^-1.
The proposed mechanism is expected to hold from 25 °C to approximately 0.5 Tm, stated as about 550 °C.
The proposed mechanism may not apply at grain sizes below 1 µm.
The proposed mechanism may not apply above 0.7 Tm.
Known lattice-distortion effects support the predicted qualitative trend.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says strengthening occurs 'without loss of ductility,' whereas the quantitative prediction permits the HEA to have up to 10% lower ductility than the baseline.

The prediction requires a 10–20% strength increase and an m increase of about 0.05–0.1, but the falsification rule requires both m_HEA ≤ m_Ni and a strength increase below 5%. Thus, outcomes that clearly violate one or both quantitative predictions may nevertheless not satisfy the stated falsification rule.
